newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Lee urges Tung to live up to words on rights.
newsitem.headline: HK's Lee urges Tung to live up to words on rights.

text.p: Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Martin Lee on Wednesday welcomed a pledge from future leader Tung Chee-hwa that there would be no Tiananmen-style crackdown there, but urged him to match his words with deeds.
"My Democratic Party colleagues and I await Mr Tung's matching words with action and leaving Hong Kong's laws on assembly and other freedoms intact," Lee told Reuters.

Tung said in an interview with Ted Koppel of the U.S. ABC News "Nightline" television programme on Tuesday there would be no suppression of protests in Hong Kong like China's bloody 1989 crackdown in Beijing's Tiananmen Square.
Lee, leader of the Democratic Party, said chief executive- designate Tung Chee-hwa's comment contradicted Tung's plans to curb civil rights in Hong Kong after China takes over.

"This is an encouraging statement from our Chief Executive Designate Mr Tung Chee-hwa which recognises the reality that Hong Kong is a free society where people regularly exercise their right to demonstrate peacefully within the law," Lee said.

"But there is a significant discrepancy between what Mr Tung is saying to Ted Koppel and what he has proposed doing in his consultation document on civil liberties and social order to radically restrict Hong Kong citizens' rights to free expression and lawful demonstration," Lee told Reuters.
Lee recalled China's parliament had declared that Hong Kong's existing laws on public order and lawful assembly would be null and void once the flag is changed at midnight on June 30.
Tung's civil liberties plan includes slapping a ban on foreign funding of political groups and making it obligatory to obtain police permission to stage protests.
